narrative: OMX30 faces a mixed open on Wednesday as continental Europe's sharp declines (DAX -1.51%, CAC -1.26%) collide with overnight US resilience. Technical setup is deteriorating: MACD crossed below signal, ADX remains critically weak at 1.7 (reducing confidence to Low per protocol), and the index sits -0.8% below its 50-MA despite holding +3.9% above the 200-MA—a classic distribution pattern. The weighted correlation signal of -0.544% and 6.46% VIX spike suggest institutional repositioning into defensive assets. While US yields fell 79bp (easing tech DCF pressure) and oil's modest +0.85% limits input cost damage to industrials, the broader theme is consolidation after a strong run. Key watch: hold above 3085 (lower Bollinger) or risk accelerated selling into technical support.
morningBrief: OMX30 likely opens -0.1% to -0.3% tracking European red across the board. Continental weakness dominates; DAX's -1.51% print and VIX's +6.46% jump signal risk-off mood despite S&P 500's +0.58% stability. Technically, the index broke below 50-MA yesterday and now faces 3085 lower Bollinger support—ADX at 1.7 is too weak to sustain directional conviction, so range-trading mentality preferred. Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) catch a small bid from lower yields (-0.79% on 10Y), but exporters (Volvo B, Atlas Copco, Ericsson B) lose traction as oil creeps higher and EUR/SEK weakens. Consumer names (H&M) pressured by weak EUR/SEK import dynamics. Watch: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET for any fresh catalyst; hold/sell into any relief bounce toward 3123–3130 resistance.
